question: You will see one image. Which of these is it most likely to be? (a) a frame from a top-budget film, a AAA game cinematic or a cinema nature documentary, (b) a stock photograph, (c) a seed catalog or textbook picture, (d) amateur generated art, (e) a real-time web 3D demo. Answer with one letter, a confidence from 0 to 100, and the one thing that most influenced your answer.

votes.answer: a, 78/100. The finely resolved rim lighting on the seedling’s tiny stem hairs was the strongest cinematic cue.
e, 85 — The localized cluster of procedural 3D soil meshes and simple ribbon grass geometry sitting on a low-detail, depth-of-field-blurred ground plane around a smooth spline stem.

a, 70. The cinematic look decided it: a 2.39-ish widescreen frame, very shallow anamorphic-style depth of field with a backlit rim on the sprout hairs, sun flare through haze and graded soil detail. That reads like a high-end CG or nature-documentary frame rather than stock, a textbook or a real-time demo.
a, 82, the precise golden rim light picking out individual hairs on the seedling.
(e) 66. The soil’s hard polygonal facets and the sun’s aberration-free synthetic bloom read as a live real-time viewport, not a filmed frame, catalog plate, or offline cinematic.
a, 84/100. The carefully controlled sunrise rim light makes the seedling read like a cinematic hero shot.
